description: The bar chart illustrates the computational cost, measured in Module Giga FLOPs, of four distinct components—grouped attention (g=3), patch attention (k=3), feed-forward, and a gray bar representing an unlabeled or baseline module—across three stages of an Audio back-end Conformer architecture, with each stage defined by its dimensionality (d) and sequence length (n): Stage 1 (d=180, n=500), Stage 2 (d=256, n=250), and Stage 3 (d=360, n=125). The vertical axis ranges from 0 to 0.3 Giga FLOPs in increments of 0.1, while the horizontal axis categorizes the three stages. In Stage 1, the gray bar reaches approximately 0.28 Giga FLOPs, followed by grouped attention at ~0.15, patch attention at ~0.11, and feed-forward at ~0.12. In Stage 2, the gray bar drops to ~0.16, grouped attention to ~0.115, patch attention to ~0.105, and feed-forward rises slightly to ~0.125. In Stage 3, all values decrease further: the gray bar is at ~0.115, grouped attention at ~0.105, patch attention at ~0.10, and feed-forward at ~0.125. The gray bar consistently represents the highest computational load in each stage, while patch attention remains the lowest across all stages, and feed-forward shows a slight increase from Stage 1 to Stage 3 despite the overall reduction in FLOPs per stage.
